## Summary
The hourly Claude issue pickup gets a session janitor:
- It archives automation sessions whose PR or issue has been merged or closed for 24 hours.
- It archives a fixer at once when a newer fixer for the same PR exists.
- It reports sessions stuck on a permission prompt: one push notification per stall, filed as an `ai:permission-prompt` issue.

`/fix-claude-pr` now runs the permission prompt report before every report.

## Changes
- `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py` (new twin, target `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py`). `classify_title` (`:244`) picks the automation titles. `classify` (`:316`) applies D7:
  - never a session that is running, working, or on a prompt (AD-27), or bound to an enabled Routine;
  - PR or issue finished at least 24 h ago, a `need_input` session included;
  - a superseded fixer, unless it waits on a question.

  `stalled_on_prompt` (`:370`) and `record_stalls` (`:401`) cover D12, marking each stall

2026-09-30T17:56:53.7776112Z   pr_body: Phase 4/4 of `docs/plans/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence-plan.md` (plan decisions D7, D12). Progress log: `docs/implement-plan/claude-fixer-unattended-convergence.md`. Final PR: #4648.

**Held for the twin sync.** Interim twin-first rule (Q40, until #4785): every `.claude/**` change is in its `workflow-templates/.claude/**` twin only. `.claude/commands/claude-issue-pickup.md` has no twin, so its new text (the full diff and its sha256) is in the twin-sync blocker comment on this PR and on #4648. Until the supervising session copies them as `[claude-twin-sync]`, the parity tests below fail, as expected. A `hold` claim on the head keeps the checker and the sweep off this PR.

## Summary
The hourly Claude issue pickup gets a session janitor:
- It archives automation sessions whose PR or issue has been merged or closed for 24 hours.
- It archives a fixer at once when a newer fixer for the same PR exists.
- It reports sessions stuck on a permission prompt: one push notification per stall, filed as an `ai:permission-prompt` issue.

`/fix-claude-pr` now runs the permission prompt report before every report.

## Changes
- `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py` (new twin, target `.claude/scripts/stale_sessions.py`). `classify_title` (`:244`) picks the automation titles. `classify` (`:316`) applies D7:
  - never a session that is running, working, or on a prompt (AD-27), or bound to an enabled Routine;
  - PR or issue finished at least 24 h ago, a `need_input` session included;
  - a superseded fixer, unless it waits on a question.

  `stalled_on_prompt` (`:370`) and `record_stalls` (`:401`) cover D12, marking each stall

| 1 | [BLOCKER] `permission_prompts.py` `_segment_credentials()` / `_segment_shape()`: the first word of a segment is taken as the command, so a wrapper hides it. `sudo mysql -pS3cretPass app` was posted as is in the example **and** in the shape (`sudo * -pS3cretPass *`), which becomes the issue title. The same happened for `timeout 30 mysql -p…`, `env curl -udeploy:pwd`, `xargs … curl -u …`, and `sudo docker login -p …`. | Plan G1 (mask `mysql -p`, `curl -u`, `docker login -p` values) and G3 (the shape never carries raw text). This is the same disclosure the issue reports, through a common command form. | New `_wrapped_command_index()` looks past known wrappers (`sudo`, `doas`, `env`, `timeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `exec`, `xargs`, `stdbuf`, …) to the first word naming a command with credential flags. 2026-09-30T17:53:33.6264318Z   pr_body: ## /verify-activation fix — issue #5124 (conformance 1/3)

Refs #5124

**Verdict on the project branch before this PR:** INCOMPLETE (scope: conformance, audited on `claude/implement-plan-issue-5124-mask-credentials-in-prompt-reports` at `6bcc3b8`). Implemented: PARTIAL (downgraded from COMPLETE by one EVIDENCE-BASED BLOCKER). Correctness: FAIL.

Plan: `docs/plans/issue-5124-mask-credentials-in-prompt-reports-plan.md`. Progress log: `docs/implement-plan/issue-5124-mask-credentials-in-prompt-reports.md`. This PR targets the project branch and runs in Claude-fixer mode like the phase PR.

## Findings fixed
| # | Finding | Why it is an issue | Fix | Verified by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | [BLOCKER] `permission_prompts.py` `_segment_credentials()` / `_segment_shape()`: the first word of a segment is taken as the command, so a wrapper hides it. `sudo mysql -pS3cretPass app` was posted as is in the example **and** in the shape (`sudo * -pS3cretPass *`), which becomes the issue title. The same happened for `timeout 30 mysql -p…`, `env curl -udeploy:pwd`, `xargs … curl -u …`, and `sudo docker login -p …`. | Plan G1 (mask `mysql -p`, `curl -u`, `docker login -p` values) and G3 (the shape never carries raw text). This is the same disclosure the issue reports, through a common command form. | New `_wrapped_command_index()` looks past known wrappers (`sudo`, `doas`, `env`, `timeout`, `nice`, `nohup`, `time`, `command`, `exec`, `xargs`, `stdbuf`, …) to the first word naming a command with credential flags. Both the credential scan and the shape use it. Only flags **after** that command

## Problem
`scripts/claude_session_janitor.py` archived an idle issue-start session whenever *any* later `implement-plan issue-<n>-… — <stage>` session for the issue was on the `list_sessions` page. That included a stage the checker archived because its start trigger failed. Archiving the issue-start session auto-disables its 24h safety net and hand-back Routines, which are the chain's only recovery, so the project could stall before its security pass.

## Change
- `scripts/claude_session_janitor.py`: `classify()` no longer collects later stages. An issue-start session is archived only when its issue is closed. Stage titles are still recognised and counted `not_ours`. `NON_SUPERSEDING_STAGE_PATTERN` is kept, commented, so no module name changes (§6). The docstring rule 2 and the API-budget text are updated.
- `tests/test_claude_session_janitor.py`: an archived (failed-start) stage, an idle later stage, and a running later stage each keep the issue-start session while its issue is open. A failed start followed by a closed issue archives it with `issue-start: o/r#7 closed`. The prefixed-stage and pickup-titles tests are updated.
